Tim Cook visited Apple's Battersea campus in London this week to meet with King Charles, as part of a new collaboration between Apple and the King's Trust Foundation.

At Apple's Battersea headquarters, Cook also sat down for an exclusive interview with The Independent to discuss this collaboration and his first month as Apple's executive chairman.

Cook stepped down as Apple's CEO last month, handing the reins to John Ternus. In this week's interview, Cook noted that the transition "actually began a few years ago."

Ternus hit the ground running with the launch of the iPhone Duo, which Cook said had been planned long in advance. Cook explained: "I wanted John to have a smooth path. And a lot of Apple's momentum comes from the product cycle."

Cook also emphasised that his role as Apple's executive chairman is now focused on "global policy," noting that there is "a great deal of trust" between him and Ternus. Cook said he would help Ternus "in whatever way he sees fit," but made clear he would "not be micromanaging."

What advice did Cook give Ternus? "Don't try to be me." You can read the full interview at The Independent, which also includes an in-depth discussion of Apple's new partnership with the King's Trust Foundation.
